text: A royal lady. <break time="0.8s" /> Had been reading the letter. <break time="0.8s" /> In her room. <break time="0.8s" /> When another important person. <break time="0.8s" /> From whom she wished to hide it. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly entered. <break time="0.8s" /> Failing to push it into a drawer. <break time="0.8s" /> She left it open on the table. <break time="0.8s" /> With the address on top. <break time="0.8s" /> The Minister D, came in and he at once noticed the letter. <break time="0.8s" /> Recognized the handwriting. <break time="0.8s" /> And guessed her secret. <break time="0.8s" /> From her nervous face. <break time="0.8s" /> Laying a similar letter of his own. <break time="0.8s" /> Beside it. <break time="0.8s" /> He later took hers. <break time="0.8s" /> And she dared not stop him. <break time="0.8s" /> With the other person present. <break time="0.8s" /> Hoping to get the letter back. <break time="0.8s" /> The Prefect had searched. <break time="0.8s" /> The Ministers house every night. <break time="0.8s" /> For three months. <break time="0.8s" /> The Minister being often away. <break time="0.8s" /> His men had opened every drawer. <break time="0.8s" /> Drilled into the legs of every chair. <break time="0.8s" /> And examined each page. <break time="0.8s" /> Of every book in the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Twice the Minister had even been stopped by fake robbers. <break time="0.8s" /> And searched. <break time="0.8s" /> But the letter was nowhere to be found. <break time="0.8s" /> When Dupin said. <break time="0.8s" /> The Minister was no fool. <break time="0.8s" /> The Prefect answered. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was a poet. <break time="0.8s" /> Which he thought was nearly the same thing. <break time="0.8s" /> Dupins only advice was to search the house again thoroughly. <break time="0.8s" /> And the Prefect left us. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking more unhappy. <break time="0.8s" /> Than I had ever seen him.
